flagged.evidence: Clause (a) says: “This unique covector is called the wave covector of θ” and explicitly allows every k∈V*. Take θ(p)=0 for every p; its unique covector is k=0, which (a) therefore calls a wave covector. Clause (c) instead defines a wave covector as “a nonzero element k∈V*,” and (d) says it “excludes the zero covector from the term wave covector.” These definitions conflict on the admitted constant-phase case.

L1 calls Λ=M^{-1} “the matrix of the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map L with Le_a=e'_a.” The opened supplier lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz, Statement (i), says “M is the matrix ... of a linear Lorentz map L ... L(e_a)=e'_a”; it identifies M^{-1} as the matrix of L^{-1}. For a passive boost β=(3/5)e₁, M=B(-β) has entry M¹₀=+3/4, whereas Λ=B(β) has Λ¹₀=-3/4. The theorem’s own step 2.3 correctly uses M=Λ^{-1}; it does not make the inaccurate fact true.

The page states: “All six items are conditional computations inside the adopted ideal plane-wave model.” The opened ex-sr-phase-level-sets-and-null-generators and ex-sr-null-covector-frame-data-worked have domain: mathematics and exclusively mathematical dependencies. The latter explicitly says “no physical interpretation of the data is used.” Their deductions require affine Minkowski geometry, not adoption of the physical plane-wave postulate; the sentence incorrectly attributes that physical premise to both mathematical examples.
